description: Verify that DUT re-picks its Link-Local address after a probing-window ARP Reply conflict (RFC 3927 §2.2.1, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 3927 §2.2.1 mandates re-pick on any conflict signal during probing — Request, Reply, or Probe. This case targets the Reply branch: an ARP Reply whose sender_proto_ip matches DUT's tentative LL also signals collision and must abort the claim.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine)

2. DUT → wire: first ARP Probe with target_proto_ip = tentative_LL

3. Tester → DUT: ARP Reply, sender_proto_ip = tentative_LL (claims the tentative address)

4. Observation:
   • DUT → wire: a fresh ARP Probe with target_proto_ip ≠ tentative_LL   ← key check

[Pass condition]
First DUT Probe AND a follow-up Probe targeting a different LL after the Reply conflict.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_initial_probe — DUT did not emit any initial ARP Probe within the deadline
• Fail_no_repick — DUT did not re-probe with a different LL after the conflict ARP Reply

verdicts.Pass: DUT re-picked its LL after the conflict ARP Reply — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_initial_probe: DUT did not emit any initial ARP Probe within the deadline
verdicts.Fail_no_repick: DUT did not re-probe with a different LL after the conflict ARP
